dedupe_keys.name: dscim spatial climate damage valuation library

description: DSCIM is the Data-driven Spatial Climate Impact Model code published by the Climate Impact Lab. Its Python library combines monetised damage estimates from different sectors with climate and economic trajectories to calculate sector-level and aggregate social costs of greenhouse gases. Users provide damage files, population and GDP series, temperature or sea-level trajectories, and choices on discounting, risk and equity. Outputs are cost estimates under those assumptions, with spatial detail inherited from the input damage data. Apache-2.0 source, package installation and a methods-oriented README are public. A limitation is that the software parses externally prepared damage estimates; it does not establish that those estimates capture all infrastructure losses or distributive impacts. It can help compare climate-policy assumptions relevant to infrastructure adaptation and equity. The catalogue's data-ipcc-ar6-scenarios-database is a separate scenario source, not DSCIM's damage dataset. No damage files or package was downloaded.
